h: Getting the Most From a Very Big Zoo
p: The honest truth about Chester Zoo is that it's too big to see properly in one go, so the smartest families pick their priorities before they set off. Write down the three or four animals everyone is desperate to see, grab a map on arrival and plan a loop that takes them in, filling the gaps as you go. Anything you miss is a reason to come back.

Some areas are worth carving out real time for. Realm of the Red Ape is home to Sumatran orangutans, with tall climbing structures that give them room to swing. The Elephants of the Asian Forest area has a large herd of Asian elephants, and watching the younger ones play in the pools is a joy. Islands is a journey through habitats from the Philippines, Indonesia and beyond, including the Monsoon Forest building, a huge indoor rainforest that's warm, steamy and a godsend when it's chilly outside.

Food and rest stops are spread across the site, but queues build at lunchtime, so eating a little early or late pays off. Bring a refillable bottle, sun cream and something for the inevitable sticky fingers.

Back in the city, the Eastgate Clock, the Roman amphitheatre and the black-and-white Rows are all a short stroll from each other. Grosvenor Park, with its play area and riverside setting, is a good place to wind down. If you've got two days, team the zoo with Blue Planet Aquarium at Ellesmere Port for a proper animal-themed weekend.
